extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of psychology, literary critics, and writers interested in the theory and technique of wit/humor
extracted.subtask_description: Theoretical criteria and technical guidelines for how wit produces laughter and how to craft witticisms so they work on an audience (psychological account linking wit-techniques to dream-work processes). Useful for analysts of humor and creators of witty material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for laughter (laughter as discharge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laughter arises when the sum total of psychic energy, formerly used for the occupation of certain psychic channels, has become unutilizable so that it can experience absolute discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hearer laughs when a sum of dammed energy in him is released and discharged; the laughter corresponds to the economy or the liberated inhibition energy (the hearer 'laughs away' the liberated amount). This framing ties pleasure from wit to release/discharge of inhibition energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why the first person often does not laugh
rubrics_metrics.description: The creator of a witticism often cannot laugh over his own wit because either the possibility of discharge is disturbed or the wit-formation itself consumed psychic expenditure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible causes: freed occupation energy attaches to endopsychic possibilities preventing motor discharge; the wit-maker expends psychic energy in producing the wit (wit-work) so no appreciable amount is liberated for discharge; attachments and lack of discharge conditions in the first person explain inability to laugh at own wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and qualifications of the third person (hearer)
rubrics_metrics.description: The third person is necessary to complete the wit-process by providing the discharge that the wit-maker lacks; the hearer must be in psychic harmony with the wit-maker and able to produce the same inhibition the joke surmounted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hearer must habitually produce the same inhibition and readiness for it (a mobilization analogous to an army) so that upon hearing the joke this readiness is recognized as superfluous/belated and discharged via laughter. 'Every witticism thus demands its own public.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of alternative outlets for liberated energy
rubrics_metrics.description: To produce free discharge through laughter it is important that the liberated energy find no other psychic use or outlet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the witticism evokes other exciting trains of thought (depending on agreement/antagonism with listener's tendencies), the witty process may receive or be refused attention; diverting other outlets is crucial for the discharge to become motor laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen and heighten the energy to be liberated (use auxiliary techniques)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is advantageous if the energy to be liberated in the third person is first strengthened and heightened; secondary or auxiliary techniques serve this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary techniques increase the sum of energy to be discharged and thereby enhance the wit effect. These techniques also may temporarily increase attention but are used to fascinate and impede its movement so the wit-process can proceed automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatism of the wit-process (keep attention at a distance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit works best when the wit-process proceeds automatically (not under direct conscious attention); attention must be kept from dominating the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical consequences: strive for shortest expression to expose fewer points for attention; ensure the witticism is easily understood (avoid mental effort or choices between paths); use artifice (omissions, façades, riddles) to divert or fascinate attention so discharge can occur undisturbed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity and 'witty' economy (economy vs alleviation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brevity and laconism are not witty in themselves; wit's economy is a particular kind of economy that contributes to pleasure but must be 'witty' brevity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While localized economy (saving particular psychic expenditure) can give momentary pleasure, lasting alleviation requires preventing the saved energy from being used elsewhere. Wit produces pleasure by relieving inhibition and diminishing local expenditure, but full pleasure often requires completion via the hearer's discharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty and surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit exerts full effect only when it is new and reaches the hearer as a surprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repetition diminishes effect because memory awakens attention and directs it to the prior hearing; witticisms are short-lived and prompt the production of new wit. Imparting wit to new hearers restores lost pleasure from novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid requiring conscious mental effort of the hearer
rubrics_metrics.description: A witticism loses its laughter effect on a hearer as soon as an expenditure of conscious mental work is exacted of him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allusions must be striking and omissions easily supplemented; if the wit demands deliberate thinking or choice between mental paths, the awakened attention prevents automatic discharge. This is the real distinction between a riddle (which demands thought) and wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of façades and syllogistical/comic façades to rivet attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Façade formations (syllogistical façades, comic façades) are techniques that rivet the hearer's attention with a task or comic surface while allowing the wit-process to proceed automatically underneath.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syllogistic façades force the listener to ponder the missing answer and thus occupy attention in a way that permits simultaneous discharge; comic façades can also supply a fore-pleasure/discharge that facilitates the wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements favoring the wit-process: nonsense, contrast, contrast of ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything that provokes interest and confusion—nonsense, contrast, and especially 'contrast of ideas'—tends to favor wit by evoking 'psychic damming' and increasing the potential discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast of ideas has been taken by some as essential to wit, though Freud sees it mainly as a means to reinforce effect. Confusion produces distribution of energy (damming) which amplifies discharge when released by wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Techniques analogous to dream-work: condensation and displacement
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit uses processes homologous to dream-work—condensation, displacement, representation through absurdity/opposites/indirect representation, and substitution—which shape wit-formation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condensation: multiple latent thoughts compressed into a single expression (sometimes via words with multiple meanings). Displacement: emphasis shifts from primary latent elements to peripheral elements in manifest wit. These processes help veil the latent formation while producing the witty surface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation through absurdity/through the opposite/indirect representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation through absurdity, representation through the opposite, and indirect representation are modes by which ideas are formulated in wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These forms are among the conspicuous mechanisms participating in wit-formation; they produce surprise/shift that can detach inhibition energy and favor discharge, similar to dream transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Janus-like double function of wit (twofold aims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit is double-faced: it contains tendencies that make possible formation of wit in the first person and tendencies that guarantee maximal pleasurable effect in the third person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One face (first-person) safeguards original resultant pleasure and involves fore-pleasure and mechanisms protecting against critical reason; the other face concerns technique that arouses the third person and provides the necessary discharge—often the wit-maker uses the hearer as a tool to provoke his own laugh.
